themes_detail.label: Root/Sewer Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus 0.5 weekly average—a 700% increase (z-score: 4.04)—suggesting an emerging underground infrastructure failure affecting East Harlem streets and potentially private properties.
evidence: 4 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score 4.04)
Complements 24 general construction/plumbing complaints LAST WEEK vs 5.8 weekly average (317% spike, z-score 8.92)
District has repeated multi-year DEP capital budget requests, indicating chronic water/sewer stress
reporting_angles: Interview DEP about tree root damage and sewer blockages—are crews responding to this week's spike? Is there a localized incident?
Ground-truth with residents on affected blocks: Are sidewalks buckling, basements flooding, or sewage backups occurring?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints hit 3 LAST WEEK versus 0.1 weekly average—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69, severity: high)—indicating possible coordinated or environmental damage to East Harlem's tree canopy.
evidence: 3 illegal tree damage complaints LAST WEEK vs 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Concurrent 700% spike in graffiti complaints (3 THIS WEEK vs 0.4 avg), suggesting possible coordinated vandalism
District budget requests include park and access improvements, indicating prior tree/green space concerns
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department: Which trees were damaged, where, and by whom? Is there a pattern or single incident?
Is this linked to the graffiti spike? Are vandals targeting trees and infrastructure together?

themes_detail.label: Plumbing & Construction Crisis
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints surged to 24 LAST WEEK versus 5.8 weekly average—a 317% spike (z-score: 8.92)—suggesting either a major building project disruption or widespread residential plumbing failures across the district.
evidence: 24 general construction/plumbing complaints LAST WEEK vs 5.8 weekly average (317% spike, z-score 8.92)
455 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (381 alterations), indicating heavy construction activity
Active 58-62 E. 125th St rezoning and 132 E. 125th St transit easement projects in pipeline
District has recurring plumbing complaints in baseline (676 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Which DOB projects are active on East 125th Street and surrounding blocks? Are construction crews disrupting utilities?
Are landlords conducting mass renovations that have exposed plumbing issues? Interview tenants about water outages.

themes_detail.label: Garbage Disposal & Street Sanitation Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked 700% (4 THIS WEEK vs 0.5 avg, z-score: 4.95) and street sweeping complaints jumped 1500% (4 TWO WEEKS AGO vs 0.2 avg, z-score: 5.67), indicating possible sanitation service failures across waste collection and street cleaning.
evidence: 4 residential disposal complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 4.95)
4 street sweeping complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score 5.67)
District's budget requests include 'Increase Graffiti Removal/Cleaning' request to Sanitation Department (recurring ask)
807 unsanitary condition complaints over 90-day baseline suggest chronic cleanliness issues
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY: Are there staffing shortages or route changes affecting garbage pickup and street sweeping in East Harlem?
Interview residents on blocks with concentrated complaints: How long have bins been overflowing? How frequently are streets swept?

themes_detail.label: Water Conservation Pressure Spike
themes_detail.summary: Water conservation complaints spiked to 6 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 0.9 weekly average—a 586% increase (z-score: 6.57)—suggesting DEP may have issued emergency conservation orders or residents are experiencing water supply disruptions.
evidence: 6 water conservation complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs 0.9 weekly average (586% spike, z-score 6.57)
Baseline of 4100 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days indicates chronic water/heating infrastructure stress
District's recurring DEP capital budget request suggests longstanding water system concerns
reporting_angles: Did DEP issue a water main break alert or conservation order in East Harlem 2 weeks ago? Check public advisories.
Are residents reporting low water pressure or intermittent supply? Interview building supers about infrastructure issues.
